text:
anya smith: quick RFC follow-up — i think we should dramatically shrink the public console query surface for view/tiles. proposal: expose two narrow endpoints from the view-coordinator: `/v1/tiles` (read-only tile fetch) and `/v1/placement` (layout hints). keep all complex fanout/caching inside coordinator.

mike chen: curious — why shrink? seems like extra indirection for panels that want full query flexibility.

anya smith: main reasons:
- stability: we frequently change internal tiling heuristics, which currently forces clients to bake assumptions. smaller surface means fewer client breaks.
- perf & caching: coordinator can maintain a KV cache + per-tenant LRU and do smart prefix coalescing (reduce downstream query QPS).
- RBAC simplification: central auth checks at coordinator reduce scattered rules across many query adapters.

shira patel: RBAC bit is important. does this mean console routes now need to call coordinator for authorization decisions instead of checking locally? that's an availability concern.

anya smith: suggestion: coordinator does primary auth check and returns a short-lived signed token for downstream adapters when appropriate. adapters only verify signature + minimal scopes. fallback: if coordinator unavailable, adapters can fall back to local policy with reduced exposure (read-only filtered result).

luis rodriguez: hmm signed token flow looks ok. need to ensure token issuance is cheap and doesn't add latency on hot paths. what's the plan for batching?

anya smith: coordinator will batch tile requests within a 5ms window (configurable per-tenant) and do continuous batching to GPU-backed query services. basic pseudocode:
```
// coordinator batching sketch
collectRequests(window_ms=5) -> groupBy(tenant, panelId)
if group.size > 1: coalescePrefixes(group)
forwardBatchToAdapters(batch)
```
This reduces per-token cost and keeps p99 latency within SLOs.

mike chen: what about debugging? Teams built dashboards assuming they can hit intermediate query surfaces for ad-hoc checks. removing those endpoints hurts debugability.

anya smith: good point — plan is to keep an "inspector" mode behind a feature flag + SSO check that allows expanded query surface for dev tenants only. it will be auditable.

shira patel: alerting/observability — we need per-tenant cost attribution still. coordinator should emit token-level metadata for billing and a request fingerprint to link to console traces.

anya smith: agreed. coordinator will propagate headers: `x-tenant-id`, `x-request-fingerprint`, `x-coordinator-token`. adaptors must emit those to traces.

infra-bot: canary rollout scheduled: eng-platform/tiling-coordinator v0.3 -> 10% traffic at 2024-12-18T15:00:00Z.

mike chen: rollout notes? rollback plan?

anya smith: rollout steps in brief:
1) enable coordinator in read-only mode for 10% traffic (no signed tokens) -> verify metrics for latency, error-rate, cost per-req.
2) enable token issuance for 10% -> adapters verify; monitor auth failures.
3) flip inspector feature to a small set of dev tenants for parity testing.
4) iterate on batching window and cache TTLs.
Rollback: switch traffic back to old router (stateless) and invalidate coordinator cache.

luis rodriguez: performance goals?

anya smith: target: p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 180ms for tile fetch across typical dashboards; cost delta <= +5% initially, aim to be neutral by improved batching.

shira patel: one last: data residency & private deployments — coordinator must be deployable in private plane and support local KMS for token signing.

anya smith: yes — architecture supports per-deployment signing keys and a config toggle for local-only caching.

mike chen: ok. i still want a short doc listing the new public API shapes and error semantics so SDKs can adapt. can you paste the minimal API here?

anya smith: pasted minimal shapes below:
```
POST /v1/tiles
Headers: x-tenant-id, x-coordinator-token (optional)
Body: { "panel_id": "string", "ranges": [ {"start": 0, "end": 100} ] }
200: { "tiles": [ {"tile_id":"t1","payload":"base64..."} ] }
401: { "error": "invalid_token" }
503: { "error": "fallback_local" } // when coordinator instructs adapter to run fallback

POST /v1/placement
Body: { "panel_id": "string", "viewport": {"w":800, "h":600} }
200: { "placement": { "rows": 2, "cols": 3, "hints": {}} }
```

luis rodriguez: thanks — looks actionable. i'll open a short RFC follow-up with the canary checklist and observability gating.

anya smith: awesome. will also add RBAC token TTL proposal and inspector feature gating to the RFC.

shira patel: acked. please cc infra/security on the RFC.

anya smith: will do. :thumbsup:
